subject: Railroad.ai — post-demo latency/throughput test plan & next steps
messages:
From: Mark Jensen <mark.jensen@railroad.ai>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>, Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 27 Apr 2029 14:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Demo earlier — follow-up on perf tests

Thanks again for the demo today — the latency and routing discussion was helpful. Our infra lead asked for a concrete set of tests we can run to compare Redwood against the hyperscaler endpoints we're evaluating. Specifically they're interested in:
- p95/p99 latency on representative traffic
- tokens/sec for short (1–3 token responses) and long (500–1500 token) generations
- behavior under bursts (microbursts)

Can you share a proposed test plan & what you'll need from our side (payload distribution, IP allowlist, preferred regions)? I attached a short request doc (infra-team).

--
Mark Jensen
Head of ML Ops, Railroad.ai
mark.jensen@railroad.ai
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: Mark Jensen <mark.jensen@railroad.ai>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>, Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 27 Apr 2029 16:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Demo earlier — follow-up on perf tests

Mark — great to hear; happy to lead the perf comparison. High-level recap + proposed next steps: 

1) What we'll measure (proposed)
  - p95 / p99 latency (client-to-inference) over 10k queries sampled from your traffic distribution
  - tokens/sec (throughput) for two canonical slices: short-response prompts (avg 16 tokens) and long-response completions (avg 800 tokens)
  - microburst resilience: 1000 qps sustained for 30s with 10ms jitter and a 1s spike to 5x

2) Test variants
  - Redwood hosted (recommended model family + quantized variant)
  - Redwood dedicated pool (same model, pinned config)
  - Hyperscaler endpoints you mentioned (we'll need exact URLs)
  - A/B with/without KV warm-up + batching enabled

3) Outputs we'll deliver
  - p95/p99 time series, tokens/sec distribution, resource utilization (GPU % / memory), and comparative cost estimate per 1M tokens
  - runbook + scripts (bench-specs.xlsx attached; automation scripts after scope is locked)

What we need from you:
  - sample payload distribution (short/long ratio, size histogram) — quickest is a CSV of prompt lengths
  - list of hyperscaler endpoints + any auth keys or allowlist IPs for test windows
  - preferred AWS/GCP region(s) for region-to-region tests (we'll mirror where possible)

Timing: we can scope the lab this week and run a first pass next Tue/Wed (PST), assuming we have the sample payloads. Neha will own config; Dev will run the automation.

Attachments: railroad-bench-specs.xlsx (bench matrices + metric definitions)

Next step: Mark — can you send the sample payloads and confirm a 2–3 hour window next Tue morning PST?

Thanks,
Ben Carter
Enterprise AE — Redwood Inference
ben_carter@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0132
From: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Mark Jensen <mark.jensen@railroad.ai>
Cc: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 27 Apr 2029 19:10:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Demo earlier — follow-up on perf tests

I'll take point on the config and test matrix. Quick clarifications: 
- Region: default to us-west-2 and us-east-1 unless Railroad prefers otherwise.
- For hyperscaler endpoints: please provide both inference URL and any per-request auth method. If we cannot auth, we can run synthetic head-to-head but results will be limited.
- For bursts, we'll run with two batching profiles: low-latency (batch size 1, max wait 5ms) and throughput (adaptive batching up to 128 tokens).

I'll push a lab runbook to the Drive link Ben shared and include the exact CLI commands we will run. Plan is: config freeze Monday EOD, smoke-run Tuesday morning, full sweep Wed.

Neha Kapoor
Solutions Engineer — Redwood Inference
neha_kapoor@redwood.ai
From: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.ai>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Cc: Mark Jensen <mark.jensen@railroad.ai>
Date: Sun, 28 Apr 2029 06:37:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Demo earlier — follow-up on perf tests

Adding some technical details we'll need and default assumptions for the scripts: 
- Warm-up: we'll run a 5-minute KV warm-up (if model supports KV cache) before measurements; suffix caching disabled for head-to-head unless you want to test prefix caching benefits.
- Batching: test sweep = [1, 8, 32] request-side batches; server-side continuous batching enabled where supported.
- Measurement hooks: we'll capture p50/p90/p95/p99 client-observed latency and server token emission latencies (time-to-first-token + per-token intervals).
- Resource telemetry: nvidia-smi sampling at 1s + runtime internals (kernel selection logs) where available.

Script stub (we'll commit to the Drive runbook):
  # run one sweep
  ./bench-run --endpoint $ENDPOINT --auth $TOKEN --requests requests.csv --batch 8 --warmup 300 --out out.json

If Railroad can provide a 1k row CSV of representative prompts (and a small set of long prompts ~100 rows), we can use those directly. Otherwise we'll synthesize to your histogram. Also attaching soc2-summary.pdf for the compliance questions that came up — please share any additional vendor review checklist items.

I'll coordinate time windows with your infra team once we get sample_payloads.

—Dev
Dev Patel
Infrastructure Engineer — Redwood Inference
dev_patel@redwood.ai
From: Mark Jensen <mark.jensen@railroad.ai>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>, Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.ai>, infra-team@railroad.ai

Thanks team — attached is a zipped set with: sample_payloads.json (1k short / 200 long), hyperscaler_endpoints.csv (urls + auth headers), and a preferred window (Tue 2029-04-30 09:00–12:00 PST). We're happy to start with us-west-2.

One ask from infra: please provide the expected public IPs you'll originate tests from so we can add to the allowlist.

Looking forward to the readout.

--
Mark Jensen
